title: Deletion SLA attestation and customer audit portal
creator: Asha Patel
description: Scope: Build an end-to-end deletion attestation system and customer-facing audit portal that proves right-to-be-forgotten (RTBF) requests were executed according to tenant retention policy, geographic residency, and SLA commitments. This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for: (1) triggering automated purge jobs (hosted/dedicated/private), (2) cryptographically-signed deletion manifests that include region stamps and a sequence of verified events, (3) an API and Console page for customers to request evidence bundles, and (4) background verification runs that assert successful purge and surface anomalies to SRE and Product teams.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Deletion orchestration can be triggered via Console and REST API for tenant-scoped RTBF with region and retention policy applied

2) Each purge run emits a signed deletion manifest containing: tenant id, retention policy id, affected object IDs (or aggregate checksums), region tag, start/end timestamps, and a verification signature
3) Signed manifests are verifiable using a public key endpoint and retained for tenant-configurable audit window (default 90 days)

4) Console exposes a customer-facing "evidence bundle" endpoint that returns the manifest and proof artifacts (checksums, job logs, retention policy snapshot) within SLA (30s for small bundles, controlled pagination for large results)
5) Background purge verification job runs nightly to revalidate manifests against stored deletion checkpoints; failures create a high-priority incident and visible alert tile in Console
6) End-to-end tests covering hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) modes exist and regression tests run in CI with sample datasets
tasks: Product: finalize API contract for evidence requests and response shape (include pagination and thumbs)
Design: create Console mockups for evidence request flow and SLA status tile
Eng (Orchestration): implement purge runner hooks to emit signed manifests and delivery to evidence store
Eng (Security): integrate HSM/KMS signing flow and publish public verification endpoint
Eng (Storage): design evidence retention lifecycle and encrypted object store with geo-tagging
SRE: add verification job and alerting runbook for manifest mismatches
QA: build e2e tests and synthetic purge scenarios including cross-region failovers
Docs: write customer-facing spec and admin runbook (Confluence + Console inline help)
comments: 2025-02-18 - Asha Patel: Initial scoping RFC posted. Goal is to reduce legal/CS time spent on RTBF evidence requests and provide a tamper-evident proof for customers.

2025-02-24 - Lina Gomez: Architecture review scheduled. Key open questions: how to represent aggregated vs explicit object lists, retention of manifests for on-prem deployments, and exportable audit formats (JSON/zip/signature).

2025-03-02 - Eng Arch (Maya Lin): Proposed approach: signed manifests using KMS asymmetric keys, manifest is small (checksum over deleted object IDs) by default; full lists available on demand with pagination. For Dedicated we will use tenant-owned KMS if available.

2025-03-04 - Legal (Jonas Reed): Confirmed minimum metadata requirements for proof: tenant id, retention policy snapshot, timestamp, region, and process owner. Suggested adding a non-repudiation signature. Needs security review.

2025-03-07 - Lina Gomez: Security review requested. Linking design mock: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COMP/Deletion+SLA+Attestation and draft API contract: https://docs.redwood.ai/api/purge-evidence (internal)
2025-03-09 - Eng (PR): Implementation spike PR open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/purge-attestation/pull/18 - includes manifest schema and KMS integration prototype

2025-03-10 - QA: Ran synthetic purge on staging tenant 'acme-inc'; manifest generated and verified via public key endpoint. Observed 1.8s median manifest generation time for 10k objects; pagination for 1M objects behaving as expected. Recording for follow-up: optimize database scan to reduce tail latency.
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: full object lists vs aggregated checksums — opted for checksum-by-default to limit bandwidth and PII exposure; customers can request full lists which are redacted and paginated.

Operational note: For Private deployments where Redwood cannot access customer data, provide a signed template and a local verifier binary customers can run to create a locally-signed manifest. This will be in a follow-up ticket.
Rollout plan: Beta with 5 strategic tenants on Reserved/Dedicated capacity by 2025-03-20, wider rollout after security signoff and a small performance tuning cycle.
